description:
Upstream's `app.suspend` (Ctrl+Z) suspends the process to the shell (like vim's Ctrl+Z). It restores the terminal to cooked mode, sends SIGTSTP, then re-enters raw mode on resume.

Our Interactive doesn't handle Ctrl+Z at all — it falls through to the Input component which ignores it.

Implement: on Ctrl+Z (non-Windows), exit raw mode, send SIGTSTP via `:os.cmd` or port, wait for SIGCONT, re-enter raw mode and re-render.

Ref: `interactive-mode.ts` L3192-3263, `handleCtrlZ()`.
title: Interactive: Ctrl+Z process suspend (unix)
